## Context

The code-review Pass-2 verifier prompt (`src/rebar/llm/reviewers/code-review-verify.md`, lines 104-105) asks `cited_reference_accurate` without saying whose citation it tests: "answer it only when the finding cites a specific `path:line`, else na (read the file to confirm the cited lines; never guess)". A `no` triggers the `veto:cited-reference-inaccurate` drop in `pass3_decide` (`src/rebar/llm/review_kernel/decide.py`). When a finding correctly reports that the CHANGE cites a wrong location (a stale line anchor in a doc, a dangling section reference), the verifier checks the change's citation, finds it wrong, and answers `no`, so the gate drops the finding exactly when it is right. This is the code-review twin of doglike-gossipy-pussycat, fixed for the plan-review prompts in af162e238a4.

Measured (method and per-case evidence in the comments): of 3,690 saved code-review results, 145 findings were dropped by this veto; 10 of those also carry `evidence_entails_finding: "yes"`; 4 of the 10 are correct findings about a wrong citation in the change, each re-checked against the reviewed revision (changes 1547, 1428 x2, 3056). On today's verifier settings the old prompt dropped the real 1428 case in 1 of 10 live runs.

## Prior intent

doglike-gossipy-pussycat's plan names this ticket and says it applies the same whose-citation scoping if code-review drops are found. The veto's purpose (epic messy-moose-jig) is to drop a finding whose own grounding is false.

## Approach

1. In `src/rebar/llm/reviewers/code-review-verify.md`, replace the 2-line `cited_reference_accurate` rule with the scoped rule the plan-review agentic verifier now carries, worded for a diff: the question tests the FINDING's OWN evidence (the `path:line` references it offers to support its claim), verified with the read-only file tools; `na` only when the finding offers no specific reference of its own; `no` means the finding's evidence points somewhere that does not show what the finding says and vetoes it; a reference the CHANGE makes (in code, docs, comments, or the commit message) is not the finding's citation, so when the finding's claim is that such a reference is wrong, confirming it is `yes`, never `no`; a corrected location the finding gives is judged as its own evidence. The line stays above the `<!--volatile-->` marker, so the cached prefix changes once.
2. Add `tests/external/test_code_review_cited_reference_veto_scope_live.py`, a live replay of a real dropped case: commit `6c8daf79457` on main (the merged form of change 1428), whose ADR 0059:132 cites `capabilities.py:186-206` for `_MODEL_ID_CAPABILITY_OVERRIDES` while the table is at line 317. The test checks the commit out as a temporary git worktree (skipping when the history is absent, e.g. a shallow clone), feeds its diff as `ticket_context`, and verifies the finding the review-bot saved for 1428 plus a control finding whose OWN evidence misquotes `capabilities.py:324-325`. It runs `code-review-verify` through `review_kernel.verify.verify_findings` + `pass3_decide` (`impact_code`) with the gate's settings from `src/rebar/llm/workflow/gates/code-review.yaml` (agentic, `standard` class, temperature 0). Pass: in a majority of 3 runs the saved finding escapes the veto and the control is vetoed. A synthetic fixture did not reproduce the drop on the old prompt (measured, in comments), so the test guards the new prompt's behaviour rather than failing deterministically on the old one.

The test is in the external live tier because the kernel enforces verifier prompt rules behaviorally, not by prompt-text grep (same reasoning as the parent).

Not changed: `pass3_decide`, the plan-review prompts, the review-bot service, Langfuse prompt publishing.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] Code-review verdict records are checked for `veto:cited-reference-inaccurate` drops whose finding reports a wrong citation in the change, with a count.
- [x] `code-review-verify.md` carries the scoped `cited_reference_accurate` rule (finding's own evidence; a wrong citation in the change that the finding reports is `yes`, never `no`).
- [x] The old prompt's drop rate on today's verifier settings is measured and recorded in a comment (bounded live runs; no deterministic failure is required).
- [x] The live replay test passes on the fixed prompt: the saved finding escapes the veto and the control is vetoed, by majority of 3 runs.
- [x] `make lint` and `make typecheck` pass.
- [x] `pytest tests/unit/test_code_review_ws2.py tests/unit/test_code_review_project_criteria.py tests/unit/test_review_kernel.py` passes.

## Testing
`pytest tests/unit/test_code_review_ws2.py tests/unit/test_code_review_project_criteria.py tests/unit/test_review_kernel.py`; `REBAR_RUN_EXTERNAL=1 pytest -m external tests/external/test_code_review_cited_reference_veto_scope_live.py` (needs provider credentials). Live runs are bounded to a small fixed number, each counted in the comments.
